# M3.2 focused real ATM10 playtest

Performed September 22, 2026, local Pacific time, with user authorization. This was the user's existing **ATM10 8.2** singleplayer world, not a synthetic harness. Environment: **Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.251 / Adoptium Java 21.0.9+10-LTS**, 534 loaded mods shown by the actual title screen.

## Deployment

Saved and exited through Minecraft's normal UI before changing the JAR. The previous `ATM-Companion-M3.1.jar` was backed up under workspace `deployment-backups/20260922-m32/`. Only `ATM-Companion-M3.2.jar` remains in the instance's mods directory. The installed 254,269-byte JAR matches the full-pack-tested and final-build SHA-256:

`393a37838bcaf9b962722b62e11df87e0ff1a6e64c0ed325cddd6a8223e21287`

The launcher reopened the most recently saved world. The client log confirms Companion **0.3.2** loaded. All commands were typed through Minecraft's normal command UI. No raw save-file edit, item transfer, crafting, quest submission, reward claim or movement was performed by the test. Setting the already-used diamond-pickaxe goal through the normal command is the only deliberate persistent gameplay change.

## Observed commands

| Command | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `/companion quests` | First Companion quest query this launch succeeded at 23:49:21.991; collector **29.0121 ms**, 66 chapters / 4,790 quests inspected |
| `/companion knowledge` | Published generation **2**, 50,000 retained / 95,541 runtime definitions, 39,992 item outputs; partial coverage explicitly shown |
| `/companion goal minecraft:diamond_pickaxe` | `already_owned`; one diamond pickaxe reserved from main inventory, no missing leaves, depth/nodes zero, operation `not_needed` |
| `/companion next` | Succeeded at 23:51:53; explains the already-owned goal and shows an alternative available quest; quest collector **24.1512 ms** |

Both quest requests showed **179 completed**, **4,400 available incomplete**, and **211 blocked/hidden/locked** quests. Availability is the adapter's documented FTB visibility/start-permission predicate and ID ordering; it is not strategic ranking. The first request preceded any Companion full-detail debug query. This is a cold Companion observation, not proof that unrelated FTB internals were completely cold after game startup.

The next-action output included the option titled “It's tough you'll need to prepare.” No quest was accepted, completed or rewarded by Companion. An existing formatting-code artifact remains visible in one other quest title; this patch preserves FTB-resolved title text and does not redesign title formatting.

## Recipe recovery preserved

At **23:46:59.407**, the installed mod detected a table replacement from **93,964 to 95,541 definitions**, invalidated generation 1 and waited for stabilization. Generation 2 published at **23:48:34.942**, without `/reload`. Its measured build values were **69,298 ms elapsed**, **3,536 ms active**, **887 slices**, **415 ms maximum slice**. The target slice is cooperative, not a hard latency guarantee. Retained coverage remained explicitly partial: 14,662 unsupported dependencies, 4,499 unknown/nonfixed outputs, 200,000 alternatives and 400,000 identities.

Client initialization took several minutes, including JEI ingredient-filter construction. One window capture timed out during loading; refreshing the window selection recovered it. No forced termination was used.

## Scope and end state

No Companion quest timeout or knowledge/plan exception occurred in these commands. Actual 0.3.2 startup recovery, first quest query, already-owned goal, and next-action quest context are verified. This does not establish deep dependency planning, full debug-export reliability, multiplayer behavior or every custom quest task. Full debug scans remain capable of truthful budget timeouts as demonstrated by the separate official-pack probe.

The game was left open, unpaused, with the successful `/next` output visible in chat. Evidence retained for distribution is limited to aggregate timings/counts and selected Companion diagnostics; no raw player world, inventory export, unrelated chat, account identity, credentials or server address is bundled.
